story: The FAA's AI traffic advisor SMART went nationwide on November 10th; on November 13th a ground stop officials say it did not cause held every flight leaving Alaska

repeat_reasons.reason: first response lacked the claimed projection; one targeted re-read confirmed the figures are absent

claims.claim: The FAA's SMART AI system is now active in the airspace of all of the nation's air route traffic control centers, 22 in all.
claims.verbatim: is now active in the airspace of all of the nation's air route traffic control centers (ARTCCs)
claims.notes: Headline reads 'FAA's SMART AI System Now Active at All 22 ARTCCs'. No fetched page names the Anchorage center as one of them; the deck must not say SMART is active over Alaska.

claims.claim: SMART was expanded nationwide on November 10th for the airspace of all 22 air traffic control centers.
claims.verbatim: So SMART was expanded for use nationwide on Nov. 10 for the airspace of all 22 air traffic control centers.
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska's News Source (KTUU)

claims.claim: The startup Air Space Intelligence designed the SMART system.
claims.verbatim: The startup that designed the system, Air Space Intelligence, or ASI,
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska's News Source (KTUU)

claims.claim: SMART was developed under a broader $875 million contract awarded to Air Space Intelligence in June.
claims.verbatim: SMART was developed under a broader $875 million, 12-year contract awarded to Air Space Intelligence in June.
claims.notes: Do not call $875 million the price of SMART alone.

claims.claim: The Air Space Intelligence contract behind SMART runs 12 years, according to AVweb.
claims.verbatim: SMART was developed under a broader $875 million, 12-year contract awarded to Air Space Intelligence in June.

claims.claim: SMART launched on September 21st in the airspace around Reagan National, Washington Dulles and Baltimore/Washington International airports.
claims.verbatim: Since launching SMART on Sept. 21 ... airspace surrounding Reagan National, Washington Dulles and Baltimore/Washington International airports

claims.claim: The FAA says SMART has helped reroute 180 flights.
claims.verbatim: the FAA says the system has helped reroute 180 flights

claims.claim: According to the FAA, rerouted flights saved an average of 10 minutes each.
claims.verbatim: saving an average of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight

claims.claim: According to the FAA, rerouted flights saved nearly 80 gallons of fuel each on average.
claims.verbatim: saving an average of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight

claims.claim: SMART centralizes 200 data streams, including weather patterns, flight paths and traffic flow.
claims.verbatim: centralizes 200 data streams
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska's News Source (KTUU)

claims.claim: House Democrats sent the Government Accountability Office a letter dated October 13th requesting an audit of the SMART software.
claims.verbatim: sent a letter to the U.S. Government Accountability Office requesting an audit of the new software ... the Oct. 13 letter said
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Audit request, not a pause request; no signer count.

claims.claim: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication the communications issues behind the ground stop were linked to the new computer system.
claims.verbatim: there's no indication the communications issues that caused the ground stop are linked to the new computer system
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska's News Source (KTUU)

claims.claim: The FAA's nationwide ground stop order came out at 11:54 a.m. Alaska time on November 13th.
claims.verbatim: The order came out at 11:54 a.m. AKST.

claims.claim: An official with Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport said all flights going outside the state were grounded.
claims.value: all flights going outside the state
claims.verbatim: all flights going outside the state are grounded.

claims.claim: Flights traveling within Alaska were not affected by the ground stop, according to an Anchorage airport official.
claims.verbatim: flights traveling within Alaska are not impacted

claims.claim: Cirium reported 670 flights sent back to the airports they took off from, as of mid-afternoon Alaska time.
claims.verbatim: 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off
claims.notes: Nationwide count at one moment (3:05 p.m.), not an Alaska count.

claims.claim: Cirium reported 157 flights redirected to a different airport during the ground stop.
claims.verbatim: 157 were redirected to a different airport

claims.claim: The November 13th stoppage was reportedly only the second time since 9/11 that all flights nationwide were grounded.
claims.verbatim: Hours-longs stoppage was only 2nd time since 9/11 that all flights nationwide were grounded

claims.claim: The FAA issued the nationwide ground stop at 3:54 p.m. Eastern time.
claims.verbatim: The FAA issued the ground stop at 3:54 p.m. ET

claims.claim: The FAA lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. Eastern time.
claims.verbatim: The Federal Aviation Administration lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday.
claims.notes: 8:15 p.m. ET is 4:15 p.m. AKST; about 4 hours 21 minutes after the order.

claims.claim: The FAA said a router sent too much data, overloading older air traffic control equipment.
claims.verbatim: The FAA said a router sent too much data, overloading older air traffic control equipment.

claims.claim: Air Space Intelligence said the ground stop was not based on or a result of the SMART system.
claims.value: not a result of the SMART system
claims.verbatim: The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines was the first airline worldwide to adopt Air Space Intelligence's Flyways technology, announced in May 2021.
claims.verbatim: Alaska is the first airline worldwide to adopt the technology.

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines said Flyways enabled it to save 480,000 gallons of fuel during its trial.
claims.verbatim: enabled us to save 480,000 gallons of fuel and avoid 4,600 tons of carbon emissions.

claims.claim: In the trial, Flyways found an opportunity to reduce miles and fuel use for 64 percent of Alaska's mainline flights.
claims.verbatim: Flyways found an opportunity to reduce miles and fuel use for 64% of mainline flights,

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines dispatchers evaluated and accepted 32 percent of Flyways recommendations in the trial.
claims.verbatim: dispatchers evaluated and accepted 32% of the Flyways recommendations.
claims.notes: Background; the human in the loop accepted about one in three.

claims.claim: The FAA says there are twenty-one air route traffic control centers in the continental United States.
claims.verbatim: There are twenty-one ARTCCs in the continental United States.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet
claims.notes: Fetched by the showrunner this run with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py (fact-checker's WebFetch got 403). Do not derive that Anchorage is the 22nd SMART center.

claims.claim: Anchorage ARTCC is the FAA's most northern and western en-route center and one of three FAA-designated Oceanic centers.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage ARTCC is FAA's most northern and western en-route center, and is one of three FAA designated Oceanic centers.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: Anchorage ARTCC's airspace spans three flight information regions totalling 2,427,971 square miles.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Domestic FIR 1,647,105 Miles² ... Anchorage Oceanic FIR 229,067 Miles² ... Anchorage Arctic FIR 551,799 Miles² ... For a total of - 2,427,971 Miles²
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: The Anchorage Domestic flight information region covers 1,647,105 square miles.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Domestic FIR 1,647,105 Miles²
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: The Anchorage Oceanic flight information region covers 229,067 square miles.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Oceanic FIR 229,067 Miles²
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: The Anchorage Arctic flight information region covers 551,799 square miles.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Arctic FIR 551,799 Miles²
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: Anchorage ARTCC operates two separate automation platforms, ATOP and MEARTS/FDP.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage ARTCC operates two separate automation platforms: ATOP (Advanced Technologies and Oceanic Procedures) and MEARTS/FDP (Micro En Route Automated Radar Tracking System/Flight Data Processor).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: Anchorage ARTCC's airspace includes more military airspace than any other ARTCC.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage ARTCC's airspace encompasses more military airspace then any other ARTCC.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

claims.claim: Anchorage ARTCC works with six international area control centers, in Japan, Russia and Canada.
claims.verbatim: interacts with six international Area Control Centers (ACCs) including: Fukuoka, Japan; Petropavlovsk-Kamchatski, Murmansk, and Magadan, Russia; Vancouver, and Edmonton, Canada.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, Anchorage ARTCC Fact Sheet

killed: Anchorage ARTCC is among the SMART centers (no page says so; inference only)
October 9th letter from more than two dozen lawmakers asking a pause (not on any fetched page)
Enstar 5 Bcf projection vs 6 to 7 Bcf target (not on the page)
runner_up_stories: FNSB 18-month moratorium recommendation (5 claims verified), Mat-Su reconsideration letter (10 verified), Enstar MEA exchange (4 verified); held in out/2026-11-18/claims_runnerups.md, not published with this deck.
